Slide.Title: obey (verb)
Slide.SlideText: obey (verb) Definition: Definition: to do what one is told to do Synonyms: Synonyms: comply, carry out Examples: Examples: Soldiers must obey their commanders. The student refused to obey his teacher. Police dogs are trained to obey without hesitation. Police dogs are trained to obey without hesitation.

Slide.Title: object (verb)
Slide.SlideText: object (verb) Definition: Definition: to say or show that one does not like, agree, or approve of something Synonyms: Synonyms: protest, disagree, oppose Examples: Examples: I objected when the waiter tried to remove my plate. Everyone voted yes. No one objected. They objected to the new rules. They objected to the new rules.

Slide.Title: object (noun)
Slide.SlideText: object (noun) Definition: Definition: something not living that can be seen or touched Synonyms: Synonyms: thing, article, item Examples: Examples: The house was full of colorful art objects. Have you ever seen an unidentified flying object? What is this object used for? What is this object used for?

Slide.Title: observe (verb)
Slide.SlideText: observe (verb) Definition: Definition: to look at carefully; watch Synonyms: Synonyms: see, notice, regard Examples: Examples: She likes to observe the people walking by. The students observed as the teacher demonstrated the science experiment. She likes to observe birds. She likes to observe birds.

Slide.Title: occupy (verb)
Slide.SlideText: occupy (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) live in or be in a place; 2) to take and control by force Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) reside, dwell, stay; 2) seize, conquer Examples: Examples: All the apartments are occupied. (live in) An architect occupies that office. (live in) The soldiers occupied the building. (seize) The soldiers occupied the building.

Slide.Title: ocean (noun)
Slide.SlideText: ocean (noun) Definition: Definition: the area of salt water that covers almost 75% of the earth’s surface; any of the five main divisions of this water, for example, the Atlantic Ocean Synonyms: Synonyms: sea Examples: Examples: Large areas of the ocean are polluted. He sailed across the ocean in five days. My house is by the ocean. My house is by the ocean.

Slide.Title: offensive (noun)
Slide.SlideText: offensive (noun) Definition: Definition: a military campaign of attack Synonyms: Synonyms: attack, assault, invasion Examples: Examples: Several soldiers were injured in the offensive. The plans for the offensive were secret. The police conducted an offensive against some drug dealers. The police conducted an offensive against some drug dealers.

Slide.Title: offensive (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: offensive (adjective) Definition: Definition: 1) unpleasant or disgusting; 2) morally insulting Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) stinky, rude, gross (slang); 2) disrespectful, uncivil Examples: Examples: The speaker’s comments were highly offensive. (insulting) Your attitude towards women is offensive. (insulting) The smell was offensive. (stinky) The smell was offensive.

Slide.Title: offer (verb)
Slide.SlideText: offer (verb) Definition: Definition: to present or propose Synonyms: Synonyms: give, submit, extend Examples: Examples: The child offered a flower to the visitor. Our host offered us a drink. She offered to let him use her car. She offered him a gift. She offered him a gift.

Slide.Title: offer (noun)
Slide.SlideText: offer (noun) Definition: Definition: something that is presented, proposed, or given Synonyms: Synonyms: proposal, suggestion Examples: Examples: He made me an offer I couldn’t refuse. Their offer to buy the house was rejected. I appreciated my neighbor’s generous offer. I appreciated my neighbor’s generous offer.

Slide.Title: office (noun)
Slide.SlideText: office (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) a room or building where business or work is done; 2) a public position to which one is elected or appointed Synonyms: Synonyms: room, bureau, shop; 2) responsibility, post Examples: Examples: The new governor has never held office before. (elected position) He wishes he had a larger office. (room) He wishes he had a larger office.

Slide.Title: officer (noun)
Slide.SlideText: officer (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) a person in the military who commands others; 2) a person with an elected or appointed position in an organization Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) commander, captain; 2) officeholder, leader Examples: Examples: The club elected a new group of officers. (leaders) A general is a high-ranking military officer. (commander) A general is a high-ranking military officer.

Slide.Title: official (noun)
Slide.SlideText: official (noun) Definition: Definition: a person with power in an organization; a representative of an organization or government Synonyms: Synonyms: representative, administrator, agent Examples: Examples: In some states, judges are elected officials. Many high-level officials attended the meeting. A government official answered the reporters’ questions. A government official answered the reporters’ questions.

Slide.Title: official (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: official (adjective) Definition: Definition: relating to an office or position; formal Synonyms: Synonyms: authorized, accredited, approved Examples: Examples: What are his official job duties? The soldier received official permission to leave. It’s official: They’re engaged! It’s official: They’re engaged!

Slide.Title: once (adverb)
Slide.SlideText: once (adverb) Definition: Definition: 1) one time only; 2) in the past Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) a single time; 2) before Examples: Examples: I’ve been in New York once. (one time) The hotel was once a restaurant. (in the past) Once, upon a time…(in the past) Once, upon a time…

Slide.Title: open (verb)
Slide.SlideText: open (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to change the position of something such as a door in order to allow entrance; 2) to start Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) unfasten, unlock; 2) begin, initiate, convene Examples: Examples: The chairman opened the meeting. (start) He opened the door, and the dog ran out. (unlock) It was warm, so I opened the window. (unlock) It was warm, so I opened the window.

Slide.Title: open (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: open (adjective) Definition: Definition: 1) not closed; 2) not secret Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) accessible, ajar, unfastened; 2) approachable, candid, receptive Examples: Examples: He was open about his problems. (not secret) The boss is an open person. (approachable) Come in, the door’s open. (not closed) Come in, the door’s open.

Slide.Title: operate (verb)
Slide.SlideText: operate (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to do work (for example, with a machine) or perform a function; 2) to cut into the body for medical reasons Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) perform, work, act on; 2) cut, perform surgery Examples: Examples: The doctor operates two days a week. (perform surgery) He can operate a forklift. (work) He can operate a forklift..

Slide.Title: opinion (noun)
Slide.SlideText: opinion (noun) Definition: Definition: a belief based on one’s own ideas Synonyms: Synonyms: point of view, belief Examples: Examples: I would like to hear your opinion. What’s your opinion of Japanese food? That’s an ugly building, in my opinion. You should express your opinion. You should express your opinion.

Slide.Title: oppose (verb)
Slide.SlideText: oppose (verb) Definition: Definition: to be against; to fight against Synonyms: Synonyms: disagree, contradict, resist, dispute Examples: Examples: She opposed her son’s decision to get married. Several workers opposed the manager’s suggestion. They oppose the plan to raise taxes. They oppose the plan to raise taxes.

Slide.Title: opposite (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: opposite (adjective) Definition: Definition: completely different from; exactly the other way Synonyms: Synonyms: contrary, contradictory, contrasting Examples: Examples: North is the opposite direction from south. My opinion is exactly the opposite of yours. They went in opposite directions. They went in opposite directions.

Slide.Title: orbit (verb)
Slide.SlideText: orbit (verb) Definition: Definition: to travel in space around another object or planet Synonyms: Synonyms: circle, circuit, revolution Examples: Examples: Many moons orbit around Saturn. It takes 165 years for Neptune to orbit around the sun. Many satellites orbit the earth. Many satellites orbit the earth.

Slide.Title: order (verb)
Slide.SlideText: order (verb) Definition: Definition: to give a command; to tell someone what to do Synonyms: Synonyms: command, direct, tell Examples: Examples: The police ordered the suspect to drop his gun. She ordered the dog to sit. The sergeant ordered the private to do push ups. The sergeant ordered the private to do push ups.

Slide.Title: order (noun)
Slide.SlideText: order (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) a command; 2) the correct or normal way things are organized or arranged Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) directive, charge, instruction ; 2) alignment, arrangement Examples: Examples: Soldiers must follow orders. (command) The library books were out of order. (arrangement) The files are in proper order. (arrangement) The files are in proper order.

Slide.Title: organ (noun)
Slide.SlideText: organ (noun) Definition: Definition: a part of the body that has a special purpose, such as the heart or brain Synonyms: Synonyms: body part Examples: Examples: The cancer had spread to several organs. Have you ever thought about donating your organs after you die? Nutritious food helps support healthy organs. Nutritious food helps support healthy organs.

Slide.Title: organism (noun)
Slide.SlideText: organism (noun) Definition: Definition: a living thing, often so small it can be seen only through a microscope Synonyms: Synonyms: animal, microbe, germ Examples: Examples: Which organism causes malaria? Millions of beneficial organisms live in the human digestive tract. Bacteria are microscopic organisms. Bacteria are microscopic organisms.

Slide.Title: organize (verb)
Slide.SlideText: organize (verb) Definition: Definition: to put in order; to put together into a system Synonyms: Synonyms: arrange, straighten, put in order Examples: Examples: The speaker organized his lecture notes. He organized his CDs by artist. She needs to organize her room. She needs to organize her room.

Slide.Title: over (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: over (preposition) Definition: Definition: 1) in a position directly above something; 2) moving to the other side of something Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) above, on top of; 2) across, beyond Examples: Examples: They crossed over the bridge. (across) She hung her grandfather’s picture over the fireplace. (above) The runner jumped over the hole in the ground. (across) The runner jumped over the hole in the ground.

Slide.Title: owe (verb)
Slide.SlideText: owe (verb) Definition: Definition: to have an obligation to repay money, a favor, etc. Synonyms: Synonyms: be bound, be in debt Examples: Examples: I never want to owe money to anyone. He owes the government a lot of money in taxes. They owe a huge amount of money on their house. They own a huge amount of money on their house.

Slide.Title: own (verb)
Slide.SlideText: own (verb) Definition: Definition: to possess or have Synonyms: Synonyms: hold, keep Examples: Examples: I don’t own any expensive jewelry. Mr. Rich owns two houses and a boat. She owns a yellow sports car. She owns a yellow sports car.
